classification.difficultyReason: Separate the actual base from its extension and, in part c, recognise that the external vertical distance is also the perpendicular separation from the upper horizontal base before applying the triangle formula.

content.prompt: Find the area of these triangles.

spec.description: Unfilled triangle with horizontal base, internal dashed altitude and a right-angle marker at its foot. Side labels follow their sloping sides.
spec.mathematics: The base is 130 m and the perpendicular height is 50 m. Retain the redundant side lengths 58 m and 112 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent givens only; the supplied area belongs in the answer.

spec.description: Obtuse triangle with restrained grey region shading, dashed external perpendicular height and dashed base extension. Two stacked dimension arrows have distinct endpoints.
spec.mathematics: The actual triangle base is 4 m and its perpendicular height is 2.5 m. The 5.5 m dimension extends from the left vertex to the altitude foot.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent givens only; the supplied area belongs in the answer.

answer.worked:
Use the actual base, $4\,\mathrm{m}$; the $5.5\,\mathrm{m}$ distance includes the extension.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{4(2.5)}{2}\\A&=5\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\end{align*}$$
